label: Government Spending
description: How India spends its public money

items.label: India's Total Union Budget FY 2024–25
items.context: The Union Budget presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman covered ₹47.65 lakh crore in total expenditure and receipts.

items.label: Annual Defence Spending
items.context: India's defence allocation, the largest budget line, covers armed forces pay, pensions, modernisation and border infrastructure.

items.label: Rural Development Budget
items.context: Covers MGNREGS (rural jobs guarantee), PMGSY (rural roads) and PM Awas Yojana (rural housing).

items.label: Railways Capital Expenditure
items.context: Record capital outlay for Indian Railways covering new lines, electrification, station upgrades and Vande Bharat trains.

items.label: Education Budget
items.context: Covers school education (Samagra Shiksha), higher education (IITs, IIMs, central universities) and mid-day meals.

items.label: Health & Family Welfare Budget
items.context: Covers PMJAY (Ayushman Bharat), AIIMS expansions, NHM and COVID-19 response infrastructure.

items.label: PM-KISAN Annual Outlay
items.context: Direct benefit transfer of ₹6,000/year to ~10 crore farmers, distributed in three instalments.

items.label: Department of Space Annual Budget
items.context: Covers ISRO's satellite launches, planetary missions, PSLV/GSLV production and the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme.

items.label: Chandrayaan-3 Mission Cost
items.context: Total mission cost for India's successful lunar south-pole lander — famously cheaper than several Hollywood space movies.
